items.title: CoSel: Cooperation as Selection for End-to-End Driving
items.summary: Cooperative driving can extend a vehicle's awareness beyond its own sensors, but existing cooperative end-to-end methods inject shared information into the planner and rely on cooperative driving demonstrations to learn how to use it. The moments in which shared information should change a driving decision are rare in such data, providing limited supervision for learning this behavior.

items.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies.

items.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode.

items.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
items.summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy.

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
items.summary: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context.

items.title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search
items.summary: Continuous-time multi-agent path finding on roadmaps (MAPF$_R$) offers a principled way to coordinate robot fleets with geometric collision avoidance, yet its deployment on industrial automated guided vehicle (AGV) infrastructures remains challenging, as highly connected and redundant roadmaps amplify both safe-interval reasoning and multi-agent interaction handling.

items.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?
items.summary: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens.

items.title: Special Report: Engineering Focus on Motion Control
items.summary: The Robot Report looks at recent advances in automation for manufacturing, from improvements in technologies and use cases to the potential of humanoids and AI. The post Special Report: Engineering Focus on Motion Control appeared first on The Robot Report .

items.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer.

items.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
items.summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment.

items.title: AvatarAnyone: Agentic Reconstruction of Mesh-Based Layered Avatars from YouTube Video
items.summary: We introduce AvatarAnyone, a method for reconstructing avatars from casual YouTube videos as layered meshes, with each garment and footwear as a separate mesh layered on top of the body mesh. In such videos, people differ in garment classes, clothing types, and layers, and each combination needs a different reconstruction. A single fixed layered reconstruction pipeline therefore fails.

items.title: Connected but Late: Sample Age of Commercial BLE Wearables under Wi-Fi Coexistence for Real-Time Clinical Applications
items.summary: Wearable sensors are increasingly being used in real-time clinical applications, such as rehabilitation robots and live therapy monitoring. As Healthcare 5.0 moves towards personalized therapies, their use will continue growing, potentially compromising communication reliability. Most wearables transmit over Bluetooth Low Energy, sharing 2.4 GHz with institutional Wi-Fi.

items.title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It
items.summary: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts.

items.title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses
items.summary: Reference trajectories are widely used to evaluate odometry and simultaneous localization and mapping systems. However, local inconsistencies in benchmark reference poses can bias such evaluations. This paper presents a place-revisit consistency evaluation method for reference poses in mobile sensing datasets.

items.title: Coordinating Perception and Planning for Test-Time Adaptation in End-to-End Driving under Distribution Shifts
items.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved significant milestones, yet its reliance on the i.i.d. assumption renders it vulnerable to real-world distribution shifts.

items.title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation
items.summary: We introduce EgoDepth-Bench, comprising 941,233 synchronized samples collected across 37 distinct physical environments. Each sample combines six calibrated RGB views with metric depth in the native fisheye view, reconstructed from five active-infrared stereo modules. A calibrated ball-bar confirms millimeter-level geometric accuracy, with a median error of 1.27 mm on a known sphere spacing.

items.title: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts
items.summary: General-purpose manipulation robots must acquire new skills over time without forgetting prior ones or retraining from scratch. We present a continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network (PNN).

items.title: Active Observation for Robust Visual Servoing in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Robust visual servoing during robotic grasping remains challenging, as approach-phase occlusion frequently disrupts closed-loop control. To address this, we present an active observation framework in which one arm of an existing dual-arm platform carries an RGB-D camera as an active observer while the other executes grasping.

items.title: Part-wise Certified State Estimation of Articulated Objects from Passive Stereo
items.summary: Robots in manufacturing often handle thin, hinged objects known from CAD models that change shape during the task, like folding cartons. Monitoring such tasks requires estimating the object's articulation state, its pose and the shape of any semi-deformable part. Learning-based estimators generalise across objects but lose precision while handling thin parts.

items.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
items.summary: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt.

items.title: ABI: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations for Zero-Shot Test-Time Guidance
items.summary: Behavior-cloning policies show strong ability in sequential control by generating coherent multi-step action chunks, yet their purely imitative objective limits zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks.

items.title: GeoMerge-OPD: Balanced Skill Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models excel at individual robotic skills, yet integrating heterogeneous skills into a single policy remains a key challenge for general-purpose robotic control, especially in whole-body tasks with differing manipulation and locomotion requirements.

items.title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
items.summary: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras.

items.title: VeriTouch: Verified Visuo-Tactile World Models that Improve Robot Policy Learning
items.summary: Scaling visuo-tactile policy learning is constrained by the high cost of real-world data collection and the difficulty of building realistic simulations. Generative models offer a scalable source of training data, yet useful demonstrations require plausible tactile feedback, temporal alignment with visual contact, and accurate actions.

items.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Precise language control requires embodied models to follow instructions governing both task outcomes and execution. Although recent methods train policies to follow increasingly detailed commands, existing benchmarks often assess instruction following alongside perception, planning, and generalization to unfamiliar scenes. Higher task success therefore offers limited evidence of closer adherence to instructions.

items.title: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can execute individual skills but fail to complete tasks that require combining several of them. In our audit of Xiaomi-Robotics-1, an estimated 43\% of failures involve choosing the wrong target or losing track of task progress. Wrapping a frozen VLA in a vision-language model (VLM) harness is a natural remedy.

items.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM.

items.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field
items.summary: We introduce CABOT, a computational model for autonomous mobile robots in which the discrete plane the robots operate on is not a passive stage but an active computing medium. In the classical Look-Compute-Move (LCM) model every increase in computational capability is obtained by strengthening the robots themselves, with lights, memory or wider visibility, at a cost paid once per robot.

items.title: LiteNWM: Efficient Latent World Models for Onboard Visual Navigation in the Wild
items.summary: Direct visual navigation policies generate trajectories efficiently but do not explicitly evaluate their future consequences. Generative navigation world models provide this foresight through visual rollouts, which are costly when evaluating multiple candidates.

items.title: RAGrasp: Geometry-Semantic Template Retrieval and Grasp Transfer
items.summary: We present RAGrasp, a retrieval-augmented pipeline for planar parallel-jaw grasping from a compact set of locally collected, grasp-annotated RGB-D (color and depth) templates.

items.title: NEXUS: Perceptive Whole-Body Control for Terrain-Adaptive Teleoperation
items.summary: Whole-body teleoperation requires a humanoid robot to reproduce a human operator's behavior even when their terrains differ. This demands that the robot perceive local terrain and adapt its posture and contacts accordingly, rather than copy the operator's motion frame by frame.
